mechanism_narrative: A 3-month cumulative decline in FEDFUNDS below 2.5% triggers a forward discounting effect, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by 0.25% in a month, the forward discount rate increases, compressing the present value of expected equity cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% in a month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in FEDFUNDS below 2.5% produces positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns by lowering the discount rate applied to equity cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month cumulative decline in FEDFUNDS below 2.5% produces positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns by lowering the discount rate applied to equity cash flows.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
